memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "From the Israelite community he is to take two male goats for a sin offering and a ram for a burnt offering. Aaron is to offer the bull for his own sin offering to make atonement for himself and his household." - Lev 16:5-6 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Aaron atones for himself and his household before he does anything for the nation.

There is an order here worth noticing. The man who would carry the sins of Israel into the Most Holy Place had first to be right with God in his own home. Not just personally — his household.

Paul saw the same principle centuries later. Writing about those who lead in the church, he asks a pointed question: if anyone does not know how to manage his own family, how can he take care of God's church? (1 Tim 3:5).

That is a searching thought for anyone who serves. It is entirely possible to be effective in public ministry and neglectful at home — to counsel others while your own marriage goes untended, to teach children in Sunday school while your own children barely see you.

This is not said to condemn anyone. Many faithful servants of God carry real sorrow about their families, and some situations are beyond our control. But the principle stands as a gentle warning: the people nearest to us are our first congregation.

Before you carry anything into God's presence for others, bring your own house.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is there a gap between your public service and your home life?
2. What would it look like to tend your household this week?
3. Who is in your "first congregation" that needs your attention?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, help me not to serve others while neglecting those nearest to me. Make my home the first place where my faith is real, and give me grace where I have failed there. Amen.
